name: Copernicium

discovery.discoverer: Sigurd Hofmann and team, GSI Darmstadt

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; observed only as individual atoms with sub-second to few-second half-lives.
notableCharacteristics: Named after astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, and theoretical predictions suggest it may be volatile enough to behave like a gas at room temperature, similar to its lighter relative mercury but even more extreme.
whyHere: Sharing mercury's filled 6d¹⁰ 7s² configuration one row down, copernicium is predicted to show even weaker relativistic metallic bonding between atoms than mercury — extreme enough that some models suggest it could behave like a gas or extremely volatile liquid at room temperature.
didYouKnow: Experiments studying copernicium atoms as they're created suggest they behave more like a noble gas than a typical metal, condensing onto cold detector surfaces the way radon would rather than the way mercury does.
genZNote: Might genuinely act like a noble gas despite technically being a metal. Breaking periodic table stereotypes one atom at a time.
